text: Ninth Sluice, fourth lane. Nan's house. Two months owing.
Six coppers by dusk. Or I take the nets.
Nan's drowned.
She drowned last month.
Drowned again. Took the money with her. Both times.
I'll drown you, you little eel! Get down off that bridge!
Dusk.
Six! We never found six in a week.
You want it found, you pay the mud. Mud doesn't do favours.
Nothing left in Ninth Sluice but buttons, Pell!
Count your own, Mags!
The old sill. Pell. You can see the stone.
It's only water.
Hold the rope.
Pell. Mouth.
It sang.
Stones don't sing. That's six coppers, that is.
What've you got, then?
Buttons!
Fifteen years old and you still track silt across my floor. Sit. Eat.
And don't tell me what you found, I can see from here it was nothing.
Nan, the old sill's bare. Right down to the stone. And Pell,
— Pell found buttons.
The old sill. Bare. Not in my floods. Not in Ninth Sluice since —
Never sing, chick. Hum if you must, and only for the house.
Chandler on the dike pays today. I'm back by dusk. And if that tithe-man comes early, you sit on the chest.
It answered you.
It's dusk's money. That's all it is.
The First Voices raised the Spires. They are not heard now.
In the last year of the old kingdom, the nine warden families found Queen Neveh past reason, and her court with her.
She sang her city into the sea.
The Nine made their Concord on what stayed dry.
This is the three hundred and twelfth year of that Concord: three hundred and twelve years, each with its tithe, and each balance carried forward.
…and the water kept its counsel.
Four coppers of that, if the rag-man's drunk. I want a half-walk for the other two.
No half-walks today.
Short a pin. Two wheels. Half the walks.
A wheel doesn't care who walks it.
I've forty grown backs it doesn't care about, ahead of you.
So sing it dry. Like they do up the hill.
Reading's today. The Helm reads the map, up at the palace. Whoever reads that map decides who gets wet.
Come dusk we'll all know what Ninth Sluice is worth.
Listeners.
The Tithe Map sets down who is sung first when the storm comes, and who after.
First Song. Second Song. Last Song.
Of the nine Spires, eight still answered. One of the eight answered badly.
By law the Helm reads the map aloud, and signs it; and the balance of that year was read on the sixth of Longdark.
Sing it flat for the lords, Lady Ione. They like to hear what they have paid for.
Is that what the song is for?
It is what today is for.
Four. The rag-man robbed us.
It cares up there.
Water doesn't care who you are.
Forty-one lines. No deed-district. No street. No name against any of it.
And it adds.
A column that adds on the first cast is either honest or very well made. Again.
Not yet reconciled.
And that girl of yours? Still climbing my rigging when the watch isn't looking?
Pumps for the low sluices. It's all written down. You need only say yes.
You will have my answer when I have read.
I know what you'll read.
Read it differently.
It is drawn, Ruel. I only read it.
People live down there, old friend.
And you will lose this one.
We go under and come up.
Helm. The Cantor's word: the water lies flat.
Ione Ilvane. You've flattened my harbour. My captains will be bored.
Yes, Kett?
The damp. It's getting into the paper.
It gets into everything.
The tithe cup. First the taster. Then the Helm. Then the guest of the reading.

Mr Kett. You have cast it twice.

A clerk who is trusted gets a clip.

text: She said dusk.
So did he.
First Song. The Steps. The harbour and the roads. The First Sluice, through the Fourth.
Second Song. The Mids, dike to dike. The Fifth Sluice. The Sixth. The Seventh —
— the Seventh.
Last Song. The Eighth Sluice. The Tenth. The Eleventh. The Twelfth.
…and the Ninth Sluice —
Lucan.
A physician! His own physician, now!
The tone came very quickly, my lord.
Nothing unheard.
Thirty days of this, then.
Dusk.
Four.
Four now. Two when my nan's back.
Two now.
She said sit on it.
Off the chest, girl.
Wait. I can pay.
Three long.
That's the Helm. The Helm's dead.
Keep your nets. Tonight.
Pell. Who reads the map now?
Helm Lucan Dask died on the sixth of Longdark, with the Tithe Map unsigned.
By law a Helm is chosen on the Still Days. There were thirty days, and a debt carried forward.
Pell… it's singing back.
